### Analysis

This is a forward-looking compatibility bug: Authlib has emitted an `AuthlibDeprecationWarning` indicating that the `authlib.jose` module will be removed in Authlib **2.0.0** in favor of the [`joserfc`](https://pypi.org/project/joserfc/) package. Streamlit's authentication layer currently imports `from authlib.jose import jwt` (and `JoseError`, `JWTClaims`) in [`lib/streamlit/auth_util.py`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/lib/streamlit/auth_util.py) to sign/decode the short-lived provider JWT used by `st.login`. When Authlib 2.0.0 is released, these imports will break and `st.login` / `st.user` will fail.

Currently `lib/pyproject.toml` declares `auth = ["Authlib>=1.3.2"]` with no upper bound, so a fresh install once Authlib 2.0.0 ships could pull in an incompatible version. Mitigation options include: (1) pin the dependency to `Authlib>=1.3.2,<2`, (2) migrate the JWT encoding/decoding to `joserfc`, or (3) support both paths via a version check (the existing `is_authlib_installed()` helper already inspects `authlib.__version__`). This is an upstream-driven change rather than a regression in Streamlit itself.

### Related Issues

- [#11364](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11364) — "You should install Authlib for me": Discusses making Authlib a managed dependency for `st.login`; relevant because the fix here will likely involve adjusting the Authlib version constraint or replacing the dependency.
- [#11391](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11391) — "Cannot use common tenant with microsoft login: authlib.jose.errors.InvalidClaimError": Another `authlib.jose`-related issue tagged `upstream`, directly affecting the same module that is being deprecated.
- [#12995](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12995) — "st.login against MSAL returns authlib OAuthError": Same area (`authlib`-backed OAuth flow in `st.login`), useful context for the broader Authlib integration.

Thanks [USER] for reporting this. I dug into it locally.

I can reproduce the `AuthlibDeprecationWarning` with Authlib `1.7.2`, and the warning is coming from Streamlit’s optional auth code path still importing `authlib.jose` for provider-token encode/decode. So there is a real future-compatibility issue here.

With that said, I don’t see Authlib `2.0` released yet, and the current auth flow still works with latest `1.7.2`. It emits a warning but does not currently fail. I am going to update this ticket to reflect this.
